Chapter 20
Document Management System
The successful implementation of a Document Management System
(DMS) project entails understanding the business needs and the business
processes of a company. The next step is to map these business processes
with relevant DMS features and functionalities. Finally, it’s also about
ensuring that the necessary DMS configuration is in place for smoothly
running the business processes.
During an implementation of Document Management System (DMS) in SAP S/4HANA,
when it’s established that certain types of hard-copy or soft-copy documents and digi-
tal assets are going to be stored in DMS, the next logical step is to have intensive discus-
sions and several workshops to agree on the DMS configuration objects. Configuration
in DMS forms the basis on which the businfess processes of the company will run. For
example, which functionalities of SAP S/4HANA will be integrated with DMS? How will
the linking between SAP S/4HANA areas with DMS take place? What is the lifecycle of a
document info record, and how can you maintain the structure, logical, and end-to-end
links of a document info record during its entire lifecycle? DMS configuration is the
first step that needs to happen in the SAP S/4HANA system. The configuration is the
backend activity in the system, which is a foundation on which the business processes
of DMS will run. Because it’s a backend activity and normally happens only once during
the DMS implementation project, a lot of thought, deliberation, effort, time, and con-
sideration must be accorded at the start of the DMS implementation project.
This chapter offers a deep-dive into the DMS configuration and gives step-by-step
instructions for setting up DMS in SAP S/4HANA. It highlights the guidelines and les-
sons learned from actual DMS implementation projects that a DMS expert needs to
consider when configuring and implementing DMS in an organization.
The chapter begins with discussing the number ranges that must be configured so
that they can be assigned to the document types later on. Creating document types
and then assigning the previously configured number ranges is covered next. A docu-
ment type, which holds a lot of information, controls, checks, and balances, is dis-
cussed in detail. A document type also holds the key document lifecycle controls
through statuses and the associated status network. The chapter then moves on to dis-
cuss the master data and the associated business processes of DMS, followed by dis-
cussing how to use the DMS search and reporting functionality. The chapter then
focuses on the associated SAP Fiori app, Manage Documents, available to create and

manage documents in DMS. The chapter concludes by showing how DMS integrates in
the QM business processes, such as in results recording, usage decision, and even
batch management.
Note
For more on DMS, see Document Management with SAP S/4HANA (SAP PRESS, 2020).
We’ll start with the basic configuration settings needed to set up DMS.
20.1 Configuration Steps
Let’s begin with the configuration details, which is the control data node. The control
data configuration node of DMS primarily controls important DMS elements such as
the number ranges and their assignments to document types. A document type itself
holds vast controls, including the SAP objects that it can link to the entire lifecycle of a
document and the fields available for changes after the document info record attains a
certain status. Here, status type is another important control that prompts or prevents
the business user from performing certain functions or actions.
Let’s start by defining the number ranges for the document types.
20.1.1 Define a New Number Range
The first configuration step in DMS is defining number ranges to be used for document
info records. When a document info record is created and saved in the SAP S/4HANA
system, the system should be able to assign it a unique and incremental number from
the number range defined in this step. There can be external or internal document
numbers. With external document numbers, the user manually assigns a number to
the document info record. Internal document numbers are assigned by the system.
The number range is 20 characters long. An important advantage of DMS is the ability
to make mixed number assignments, that is, internal as well as external numbers.
When a user assigns an external number to a document info record, the system auto-
matically adds an internal number to it.
During the course of a DMS implementation, the client and the DMS expert agree and
decide on what numbers and ranges of numbers are allowed. After the number ranges
are defined, these are then assigned to the document types that we’ll discuss in the
next section.
To define a new number range for a document info record, follow the menu path SAP
IMG  Cross-Applications Components  Document Management  Control Data  Define
Number Ranges for Document Numbers. A list of existing number ranges, shown in
Figure 20.1, will appear.

20.1.2 Defining the Document Type
Defining and configuring document types is one of the important configuration steps
in DMS. The document type is highly relevant to business users and is the first thing
they select when creating a document info record. A document type (denoted with
three alphanumeric characters) holds a large number of associated controls and func-
tionalities, including the following:

20 Document Management System
858
 Status networks
 Additional attributes used for searching
 Object linking
 Conversion processes for creating neutral files
 Security through roles and authorizations
During a DMS implementation, a lot of discussion and deliberation takes place
between the DMS expert and the client’s business users to maintain a fine balance of
defining document types that meet the business requirements and reporting needs.
This fine balance ensures that not too many or too few configuration objects, which, in
this case, refer to the document types, are created. Creating too many configuration
objects becomes confusing and cumbersome for business users to enter or maintain all
the data. Creating too few configuration objects risks losing the depth and breadth
required to truly benefit from DMS.
To create a new document type, use Transaction DC10 or follow the menu path SAP IMG 
Cross-Applications Components  Document Management  Control Data  Define DMS
Document Types (see Figure 20.3).
The document type configuration consists of the following three steps:
1. Create the initial document type.
2. Define the status network.
3. Define which object links are relevant for the document type.
Figure 20.3 shows several document types available in the standard SAP S/4HANA sys-
tem. To create a new document type, we recommend copying an existing document
type to save time and maintenance. For this example, use the standard available docu-
ment type DRW to create a new document type QM1. Select document type DRW, and
choose the Copy As function in the menu bar.

20.1.3 Document Status
The next step in configuring a document type is defining the status network for the
document type. A status network denotes the lifecycle of a document info record. Let’s
demonstrate a status network with an example and for the document type QM1. A doc-
ument info record of document type QM1 will start with an initial status of In Work and
will then be allowed to proceed to the Under Review status. From Under Review, it can
move back to In Work or move forward (the next step) to Released. The Released status
signifies that the document info record is released, and a revision level can be assigned,
if needed. If the document info records are expected to be eventually archived, then the
fourth status can be Archived.
Let’s now configure this status network for document type QM1. With document type
QM1 open, in the Dialog Structure pane located on the left side of the screen, choose
Define document status. Figure 20.6 shows an overview of available statuses with a sta-

all statuses that aren’t needed.

Tips and Tricks
Some DMS implementation tips and tricks related to document status are as follows:
 It’s highly recommended to keep the same two-letter alphanumeric status identifi-
cation for the Document Status and Status fields shown earlier so it’s easier to
understand what each status means and signifies. In this example, we maintained
“UR” for both of them.
 Notice that there’s no provision to enter the description or the text of a status. This
option is available and should be used by choosing Define document status
descriptions from the left side panel in Figure 20.6.
 Statuses aren’t document type-dependent and can be maintained in multiple lan-
guages. A good implementation approach can be to define all the different docu-
ment statuses (in a single language or multiple languages, if needed) and then
assign them to individual document types to create a status network.
Table 20.4 lists the available status types that also act as controlling functions. For
example, status S doesn’t allow any changes to be made to the document info record,
whereas status C ensures that all original files in the document info record are checked
into the document repository before the document info record is saved.

be linked into a document lifecycle. This means that the doc-
ument info record can be given this status again at a later

created. It can’t be set at a subsequent stage of processing.

20.1.4 Object Links
Object links are highly useful because they make document info records visible and
available in many different transactions across the SAP S/4HANA system, such as in a
material master record, quality info record, or sales order item. An object link serves to
© 

867
20.1 Configuration Steps
link or cross-link a document info record with one or more SAP objects, such as a mate-
rial master, sales order item, and quality notification, among others. This means that
both the data in the original document info record and the originals are available in the
SAP objects.
Some features and functionalities of an object link include the following:
 An object link refers to the SAP table and the corresponding screen number.
 A document info record can either be created directly from the object link or by
using a transaction.
 An object link can be restricted so that a document info record can either be
assigned to only one record or multiple master records.
 All versions or only the current version of an object link can be displayed.
 Setting up a deletion lock can prevent deletion of a document info record if an object
link is maintained.
 Additional functions of an object link, such as classification, long text, and addi-
tional objects, can be set for providing more details about an object link.
 When creating a new version of a document info record, controls can be set if the
corresponding object links are also copied automatically, or they can be ignored.
It’s possible to link a single document info record to many SAP objects. One document
type can have multiple object links. For example, document type QM1 can have object
links to both the material master and purchase requisition item in materials manage-
ment (MM), whereas DMS document type Z02 can have an object link to change num-
bers only.
Access Figure 20.9 by choosing Define object links from the side panel for the document

belong to document type QM1. Let’s evaluate the available option in an object link.

20.1.5 Define Workstation Application
The general data configuration node of DMS primarily controls how the system will
process the document info records, as well as how it will display and print the originals.
Here, the most important settings are related to workstation applications that need to
be carefully understood and then configured because they control the different types
of files and their associated applications that can be processed within the document
info records, including websites.
Let’s begin with the necessary configuration within the control data node. When an
original file is stored in a document info record, one of the first requirements is to asso-
ciate that file to a workstation application. The workstation application controls how
original files are processed. More specifically, it controls which application is started
when displaying or changing an original file and how the original file is printed.
During a DMS implementation project, a workstation application has to be defined for
each application file type that is to be stored in DMS. For example, if a company wants
to store Microsoft PowerPoint files in the document info records, a workstation appli-
cation has to be defined so it can be selected when a user checks in a Microsoft Power-
Point file. The selection of the workstation application is based on the extensions of the
Microsoft PowerPoint file, that is, .ppt or .pptx. Further, in configuration, it can be spec-
ified that the Microsoft PowerPoint application launches whenever someone changes
or displays a Microsoft PowerPoint file that is associated with a document info record.
We’ll show the entire configuration with an example by discussing the settings for the
workstation application DOC, for Microsoft Word documents. After the necessary
understanding is developed, additional workstation applications required for the DMS
project can be configured. Apart from the workstation DOC, SAP provides additional
standard applications in the system.
To set up the workstation application and the associated configuration settings involved,
follow the menu path SAP IMG  Cross-Applications Components  Document Manage-
ment  General Data  Define Workstation Application.

20.2.1 Creating a Document Info Record
Documents created in DMS are referred to as document info records. A document info
record is the master record in the SAP S/4HANA system. It manages the originals and
controls workflows. An original is the actual file information retained in the document
info record. An original can be a Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel file, a PDF docu-
ment, a design drawing in 2D or 3D format, a website, or even a text file. The storage
location of an original is also maintained in the document info record. Document info
records contain all the information as well as the control functions and features. In the
SAP S/4HANA system, DMS uses a document info record to link the document to an
SAP object, such as a material master or equipment.
Before delving into document info record creation in the SAP S/4HANA system, let’s
first gain an understanding of the key concepts and terminologies that you’ll see in this
section:
 Document types
A document type is three alphanumeric characters with number ranges (internal or
external) that act as a distinguishing feature of the business process. The document
type controls the major functions. An example of a document type is ZQM, which
stores all documents related to a supplier’s quality certification process. When creat-
ing, changing, or displaying a new document info record, it’s mandatory to enter the
relevant document type.
 Document part
A document part is defined as part of a document info record that is maintained as a
separate document. This separation may be required if the original document is
large and can be divided into relevant sections. For example, a large specification
document has relevant information for many materials; the specification can be
divided into separate parts for each material. As an example, an individual design or
an engineering drawing of a product may have several complex parts, making it
practical to divide them into document parts. A document info record can have up
to 999 parts.
 Document version
A document version describes the version number of a document info record. This
number is particularly important for keeping the document current in situations
where modifications may have been made to specifications, engineering drawings,
and so on. A document info record can have up to 99 versions.
 Document statuses
All major activities and even controls in a document info record are undertaken and
managed based on document statuses. Some examples of user-defined document
statuses include In Process, Under Review, Released, Locked, and Archived.

When a document info record is going through several rounds of review and approval

business functions. For example, a Released status of the document info record

the document info record are no longer possible. Similarly, a document info record
with the status of Locked is available, thereby ensuring no further inadvertent use of
the document info record. Whenever a document status is changed, a complete change
history is maintained.

20.9 Summary
In this chapter, we covered DMS configuration in sufficient detail. By now, you’ve
gained a good understanding of the concepts and steps necessary to configure number
ranges, document types, lab offices, and several other configuration items. With the
configuration complete, the necessary baseline to begin using DMS in SAP S/4HANA is
in place. In terms of an actual and real-life DMS implementation project, it’s recom-
mended to refer to and even revisit the DMS configuration topic throughout the lifecy-
cle of the project.
We also described the business processes of document info record management. Most
companies have developed or are still developing strategies regarding their docu-
ments. Having hard-copy documents moving around an organization can cause
delays, errors, and miscommunication. Scanning documents on receipt (e.g., invoices
from vendors) is one way to reduce the time between approvals and payments to ven-
dors. Knowledge of DMS in SAP S/4HANA is paramount when advising clients on the
best practices for purchasing and other areas where management of documents and
digital assets can be an issue.
As we come to the end of this book, you’ve seen that the QM area in SAP S/4HANA is
quite comprehensive and offers in-depth and practical solutions for many business
processes and scenarios in a diverse range of industries. Not only that, it offers options
that enable you to implement and integrate QM into all your important business pro-
cesses. However, the actual return on investment for the SAP S/4HANA implementa-
tion can be ensured only when you strive to understand the integration of various SAP
areas and functionalities with each other. To achieve flawless integration during an SAP
S/4HANA system implementation, you need to maintain extensive collaboration and
intense coordination among the various stakeholders of the company.
